'''''Juncus bufonius''''', known commonly as '''toad rush''', is a widespread [[flowering plant]] [[species complex]] in the rush family [[Juncaceae]].<ref name=grin>[https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?316713 GRIN-Global Web v 1.9.4.2: Taxonomy of '' Juncus bufonius'']</ref><ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=JUBU USDA: ''Juncus bufonius'']</ref><ref name=jepson>[https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=29618 Jepson: ''Juncus bufonius'']</ref>

==Distribution==
Its native range is circumpolar throughout [[tropical]], [[subtropical]], [[subarctic]], and [[temperate climate]] areas of the [[Northern Hemisphere]] and [[Southern Hemisphere]].<ref name=grin/><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200027401 Efloras.org:  ''Juncus bufonius'' in Flora of North America]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200027401  Efloras.org:  ''Juncus bufonius'' in Flora of China]</ref><ref name=efloraspak>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=5&taxon_id=200027401 Efloras.org:  ''Juncus bufonius'' in Flora of Pakistan]</ref><ref>[http://www.alocasia.com.au/qld_saltmarsh_plants/herbarium/grasses-rushes-and-sedge-plants/toad-rush Online Field Guide to Common Saltmarsh Plants of Queensland]</ref>
<ref>[http://www.hear.org/pier/species/juncus_bufonius.htm PIER Profile: ''Juncus bufonius'']</ref> 
It is also widely distributed as an introduced species in suitable habitats worldwide.  It grows in moist and muddy places, often in [[wetland]]s and [[riparian zone|riparian]] areas.<ref name=calflora>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Juncus+bufonius   Calflora: ''Juncus bufonius'']</ref>

In [[habitat]]s where it is not native and has [[naturalized]] it may be considered a weed. The relationship of North America plants to the Eurasian ''[[Juncus ranarius]]'' is weakly delineated.<ref name=jepson/>

==Description==
''Juncus bufonius'' is an annual [[Monocotyledon|monocot]] that is quite variable in appearance.    It is generally a green clumping grasslike [[Juncus|rush]], with many thin stems wrapped with few threadlike leaves.<ref name=jepson/>

The flowers are borne in inflorescences and also in the joint where the inflorescence branches off of the stem. It is a grassy flower folded within tough bracts and sepals.<ref name=jepson/> The blooming period is March to May in the Northern Hemisphere and September to November in the Southern Hemisphere.<ref name=calflora/>
